Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Building a Support Network and Enlisting Allies.
If you think about moving forward in your career, one thing keeps coming up—the power of relationships. Not just for the company or the friendship, but as real sources of support, advocacy, and new opportunities.
Now, so many women are amazing at forming strong, genuine connections, but sometimes there’s a little hesitation when it comes to turning those relationships into something strategic.
Here’s the thing: Enlisting allies isn’t about collecting business cards or keeping score. It’s really about building relationships that are genuine and go both ways. Your allies might be mentors, sponsors, peers, or even folks outside your immediate field. What really matters is that they can offer fresh perspective, open doors you didn’t even know existed, and advocate for you—especially when you’re not in the room.
So, how do you actually build and activate this kind of support network? Let’s break it down.
First, look for people who have influence or just a unique insight, and find real opportunities to connect. It’s not about forcing it—it’s about being authentic.
Next, offer your own support. When you show up for others and add value, you’re building a foundation of trust and mutual respect.
Be open about your goals and dreams. If your allies know where you want to go, they’ll know exactly how to help you get there.
And don’t be shy about asking for an introduction, some honest feedback, or a little advocacy when you need it. You might be surprised—most people are happy to help when you just ask.
Imagine your network as a garden. It needs attention, a bit of variety, and, of course, some time to really grow. When you invest in these relationships and enlist true allies, you’re building a web of support that can keep you moving forward—and even help you make leaps you never saw coming.
